name: MuleSoft, LLC (formerly MuleSource; owned by Salesforce)
origin_detail: Ross Mason started the open-source Mule ESB project in 2003; he and Dave Rosenberg founded the company in 2006 (briefly Azechi, Inc., then MuleSource LLC, renamed MuleSoft in 2009), headquartered in San Francisco
openness_notes: Began as an open-source ESB (Mule Community Edition) with a paid Enterprise Edition (open core). The business shifted to the proprietary Anypoint Platform, and on 18 Sep 2026 the Mule Community Edition repository was archived (read-only) under Salesforce. Rated 1 now: the live product is proprietary and only legacy/peripheral code is public. The CE licence (commonly reported as CPAL) was not confirmed in fetched pages.

license_history.license: Open source (Mule ESB Community Edition; licence not confirmed in fetched pages)

relicensing_events.to: Archived community repository; proprietary Anypoint/Enterprise only
relicensing_events.outcome_note: End of maintenance rather than a relicence; repository has 688 forks but no major community fork identified

exit_events.note: Priced 16 Mar 2017 at $17 (above $14-16 range), 13M shares (~$221M gross); first-day close $24.75 (+45%); 2016 revenue $188M (+70%), net loss $50M
Agreed Mar 2018, completed May 2018; cash-and-stock deal reported at ~$6.5B

risk_events: Loss-making at IPO and in 2017 (net loss $80M on $296M revenue)
Absorbed into Salesforce (2018); independent brand continues inside Salesforce
18 Sep 2026: Mule Community Edition repository archived (read-only), ending the open-source line
robustness: Commercially robust as a Salesforce product line (1,400+ employees and 1,600+ customers by Aug 2019). The open-source heritage is now weak: the community edition is archived, so users of the free runtime have no maintained upstream unless a fork emerges.
openness_effect_assessment: Open-source Mule built early developer adoption and credibility in a market dominated by proprietary ESBs, but growth to a $6.5B exit came from the proprietary Anypoint Platform. Openness was a go-to-market phase rather than the long-term model, and under Salesforce the open edition was eventually archived.
key_takeaway: MuleSoft is the 'open-source on-ramp' case: a community project (2003) became open core, then a proprietary platform that IPO'd (2017) and sold to Salesforce for $6.5B (2018). The open edition was archived in 2026, illustrating how openness can fade once a big-company parent controls the product.
